senses.definition: A tree that produces acorns and usually has very hard wood.
senses.example: The old oak gave us shade all afternoon.

senses.definition: A long tool with a flat end used to move a boat by pushing against water. It often rests in a holder on the boat.
senses.example: We pulled both oars to turn the rowboat.

senses.definition: A place in a desert where water can reach the surface and plants can grow.
senses.example: Palm trees grew beside the water at the oasis.

senses.definition: Oats that have been ground, crushed, or cut, or a soft breakfast dish made by cooking oats.
senses.example: I put chopped apples and cinnamon on my oatmeal.

senses.definition: Willing to follow someone's rules or directions.
senses.example: The obedient dog sat when I asked it to.

senses.definition: To do what a rule, instruction, or person in charge tells you to do.
senses.example: We obeyed the sign and stayed off the wet floor.

senses.definition: A thing that you can see or touch.
senses.example: One small object in the box was a silver button.

senses.definition: To say that you disagree with an idea or plan.
senses.example: I objected to skipping Mira’s turn in the game.

senses.definition: A statement that you are against a plan, idea, or action.
senses.example: One objection to the new play area was that it blocked the path.

senses.definition: Not well known or difficult to understand.
senses.example: My cousin collects old books about obscure games whose rules most people have forgotten.

senses.definition: To block or hide part or all of a view.
senses.example: Fog obscured the tops of the trees.

senses.definition: A detail or fact noticed by watching, listening, or examining closely.
senses.example: My first observation was that the puddle was smaller after lunch.

senses.definition: To look at or notice something carefully, often to learn about it.
senses.example: We observe the shadow each day to see how its length changes.

senses.definition: To follow a rule or take part in a custom.
senses.example: The family observes the holiday by sharing a meal.

senses.definition: To get something, especially by taking action or making an effort.
senses.example: We obtained a large map from the park office.

senses.definition: A particular time when something happens, especially an important or special event.
senses.example: The class reunion was an occasion for old friends to see one another.

senses.definition: To fill or use a place or time.
senses.example: Three people occupied the wooden bench by the door.

senses.definition: To happen or take place.
senses.example: The loudest part of the show occurred just before the lights went out.

senses.definition: A huge connected body of salt water. Earth’s ocean is often divided into five named oceans.
senses.example: Waves moved across the ocean during the storm.

senses.definition: Unusual or unexpected.
senses.example: We heard an odd tapping sound in the hallway.

senses.definition: Left alone without a matching partner.
senses.example: One odd sock was still in the basket.

senses.definition: Having a whole-number value that cannot be divided into two equal whole-number parts.
senses.example: Nine is an odd number.

senses.definition: A whole number that leaves one item without a partner when you put the items into pairs.
senses.example: Nine is an odd number because one item is left after you make four pairs.

senses.definition: A smell, often one that is strong or unpleasant.
senses.example: A sweet odor drifted from the flower bed.

senses.definition: To make someone feel upset, insulted, or disrespected.
senses.example: I did not mean to offend her when I laughed at the name of the game.

senses.definition: To say that you are willing to give something or do something for someone.
senses.example: Lina offered to help carry the groceries.

senses.definition: A suggestion to give something or make a deal.
senses.example: I thanked Sam for the offer to share his umbrella.

senses.definition: A room or building used for work that often includes writing, calls, or records.
senses.example: We returned the visitor badge to the school office.

senses.definition: A position of responsibility, especially in a group or government.
senses.example: Maya ran for the office of class president.

senses.definition: A person with an official job or rank in a group, government, or public agency.
senses.example: The club elected a new officer to keep track of its meetings.

senses.definition: The young or children of a person, animal, or plant.
senses.example: The mother swan stayed near her offspring as they swam.

senses.definition: Many times or regularly.
senses.example: We often walk to the park after lunch.

senses.definition: A liquid that does not mix well with water, such as the kind used for cooking or for making machine parts move smoothly.
senses.example: We poured a little oil into the pan before adding the onions.

senses.definition: To put oil on something.
senses.example: The repair person oiled the squeaky hinge.

senses.definition: Good enough, allowed, or doing all right.
senses.example: The small crack in the cup made me wonder if it was still okay to use.

senses.definition: Used to say yes, agree, or show you understand.
senses.example: “Okay,” said Mara, “I’ll meet you by the clock.”

senses.definition: To say that an idea or plan is allowed to go ahead.
senses.example: The teacher okayed our plan to read outside.

senses.definition: Having lived or existed for a long time.
senses.example: We found an old sofa in the attic.

senses.definition: Having lived or existed for a stated amount of time.
senses.example: The puppy was five months old when we got her.

senses.definition: From an earlier time, even if it is still fairly new.
senses.example: I gave my old team shirt to my cousin.

senses.definition: A forest that has grown long enough to develop features such as large old trees and wood that has slowly built up on the ground.
senses.example: Fallen logs and very large trees were both common in the old growth forest.

senses.definition: A small fruit with a hard pit, eaten after it is treated or pressed to make oil.
senses.example: We put sliced olives on the pizza.

senses.definition: A dark yellowish green, like the color of some olives.
senses.example: My backpack is olive with a bright orange strip.

senses.definition: A dish made by mixing eggs and cooking them in a pan, often around a filling.
senses.example: I folded the omelet over the mushrooms.

senses.definition: To leave out something instead of including it.
senses.example: You can omit the pepper if the soup already tastes spicy.

senses.definition: Because you meant to do it, rather than by accident.
senses.example: The artist left the top corner blank on purpose.

senses.definition: Still deciding between two choices or opinions.
senses.example: I am on the fence about which book to take on the trip.

senses.definition: Here is a different side or way of thinking about the same problem.
senses.example: The hill is steep. On the other hand, the steep path is shorter.

senses.definition: Understanding a situation in the same way or agreeing on what to do.
senses.example: We read through the rules together to make sure everyone was on the same page.

senses.definition: Very seldom or hardly ever.
senses.example: Once in a blue moon, we have pancakes for dinner.

senses.definition: The number that means a single item.
senses.example: I rolled a one on the first turn.

senses.definition: A person or thing spoken about without repeating its name.
senses.example: I dropped my pencil, so Kai gave me another one.

senses.definition: A round underground part of a plant with layers and a strong smell and taste, used as food.
senses.example: I chopped an onion for the soup.

senses.definition: There is just one, with no other of the same kind.
senses.example: The only table left was by the window.

senses.definition: Just, with nothing else added.
senses.example: I have only two pages left to read.

senses.definition: Forward or on to the next place or part of something.
senses.example: After a snack we walked onward to the lake.

senses.definition: Made of material that light cannot pass through so that you cannot see through it.
senses.example: The opaque card blocked the light from the window.

senses.definition: Allowing someone or something to enter, leave, or pass through.
senses.example: The side gate was open, so we could take the wagon through.

senses.definition: Ready to be used or ready to serve people.
senses.example: The library is open until six.

senses.definition: To move a lid, door, or other cover so a space can be reached.
senses.example: I opened the envelope to read the card.

senses.definition: A gap or hole through which something can pass.
senses.example: The mouse found an opening beside the pipe.

senses.definition: The beginning part of an event or work, or an available job or space.
senses.example: The opening of the film showed a small boat at sea.

senses.definition: Moving something so a place can be reached, or starting something. This is the -ing form of “open.”
senses.example: I was opening the window to let in some fresh air.

senses.definition: A story performed onstage mainly through singing and music.
senses.example: We could read the opera’s story before the singers came onstage.

senses.definition: A collection of programs that helps apps and physical computer parts work together.
senses.example: The operating system tells different apps how to use the speaker.

senses.definition: What someone thinks or believes about something.
senses.example: My opinion is that the blue poster is easier to read.

senses.definition: A chance to do something you want to do or can learn from.
senses.example: The club gave me an opportunity to try painting with watercolors.

senses.definition: The next best choice you miss because you choose something else.
senses.example: My opportunity cost of choosing a train ride was missing the boat tour.

senses.definition: Across from something, or as different from it as possible.
senses.example: Nell sat on the opposite side of the table.

senses.definition: Something that is completely different from another thing in some way.
senses.example: The opposite of empty is full.

senses.definition: The bundle of nerve fibers that carries signals from an eye to the brain.
senses.example: Signals about the picture leave the eye through the optic nerve.

senses.definition: A process in which a computer looks at pictures of writing and works out which letters and words they show.
senses.example: Optical character recognition let me search an old newspaper for a name.

senses.definition: One thing you can choose among two or more choices.
senses.example: The cheapest option was taking the bus.

senses.definition: An animal bone or turtle shell used to ask questions about the future in ancient China.
senses.example: A writer cut signs into an oracle bone.

senses.definition: A story, song, saying, or other practice passed on by speaking, singing, or listening.
senses.example: Grandma learned the song from her parents as part of her family’s oral tradition.

senses.definition: The path an object follows as it travels around another object in space.
senses.example: Earth takes about one year to go around its orbit.

senses.definition: To travel around another object in space.
senses.example: The Moon orbits Earth.

senses.definition: A place where many trees are grown for fruit or nuts.
senses.example: We picked several kinds of apples in the orchard.

senses.definition: A group of musicians who play different instruments together, often led by a conductor.
senses.example: In the orchestra, the strings began the tune and the woodwinds answered.

senses.definition: The way things are arranged or the sequence they come in.
senses.example: Put the cards in order from smallest to largest.

senses.definition: A command that someone is expected to follow.
senses.example: The captain gave the order to stop the ship.

senses.definition: To ask for something to be prepared or sent to you.
senses.example: We ordered two bowls of soup.

senses.definition: Two numbers written in a set order, often used to name a spot on a grid.
senses.example: The ordered pair (2, 4) gives the sideways move first and the upward move second.

senses.definition: Usual, or like what you see or expect most of the time.
senses.example: We made the toy from an ordinary cardboard box.

senses.definition: A body part made of tissues that work together to do one or more jobs.
senses.example: The heart is an organ that pumps blood.

senses.definition: To arrange things in a clear, useful way or plan an activity so it can happen.
senses.example: We organized the books by topic before putting them on the shelf.

senses.definition: The art of making figures or shapes by folding paper.
senses.example: We learned to make an origami bird from a square of paper.

senses.definition: Early or first, rather than changed or copied later.
senses.example: The artist hung the original painting beside two prints.

senses.definition: New and thought up by the person who made it.
senses.example: Nina made up an original game for the sleepover.

senses.definition: The first version of something that was later copied or changed.
senses.example: We scanned the photo so we could keep the original safe.

senses.definition: An object used to decorate something.
senses.example: The glass ornament hung from a high branch.

senses.definition: To decorate an object or place by adding designs or objects.
senses.example: They ornamented the wooden box with carved stars.

senses.definition: A child or young animal whose parents have died.
senses.example: In the story, the orphan went to live with her aunt.

senses.definition: Different from the one or ones already mentioned.
senses.example: The other door leads to the stairs.

senses.definition: Someone or something else, especially from a set already mentioned.
senses.example: Two of us got water while the others set up the game.

senses.definition: If something else does not happen or is not done.
senses.example: Bring your hat. Otherwise your ears might get cold.

senses.definition: In other ways or apart from one detail.
senses.example: The book had a torn cover but was otherwise fine.

senses.definition: An animal with fur, webbed feet, and a long body that swims well and often feeds on fish or other water animals.
senses.example: The otter popped its head out of the water near the bank.

senses.definition: A unit used to measure weight; in the everyday U.S. system, there are sixteen ounces in one pound.
senses.example: The small bag of nuts weighed one ounce.

senses.definition: What happens in the end as a result of an action or event.
senses.example: We guessed the outcome of the race before watching the final lap.

senses.definition: To do something better or achieve more than someone else.
senses.example: We tried to outdo each other by building the tallest tower.

senses.definition: The exposed layers on the outside of a woody stem or trunk.
senses.example: Thin parts of a paper birch's outer bark sometimes curl back.

senses.definition: The far part of a baseball or softball field beyond the area around the bases.
senses.example: The ball flew past the runner and landed in the outfield.

senses.definition: A group of clothes and other things worn together.
senses.example: I chose a warm outfit for the windy day.

senses.definition: To supply someone or something with clothes or equipment they need.
senses.example: We outfitted our raft with extra ropes and a small paddle.

senses.definition: Friendly and comfortable meeting new people.
senses.example: My outgoing cousin was the first to introduce herself.

senses.definition: Going away or being sent out.
senses.example: We put our outgoing letters in the mailbox.

senses.definition: To get too big for something or stop being interested in it as you grow older.
senses.example: I had outgrown my rain boots by spring.

senses.definition: A short trip taken for enjoyment.
senses.example: Our class had an outing to the science center.

senses.definition: A line around the outside of a shape or object.
senses.example: I traced the outline of my hand on the paper.

senses.definition: A short plan listing the main parts of a talk, report, or story.
senses.example: We wrote an outline before starting our report.

senses.definition: To draw the outside line or list the main points of something.
senses.example: Our teacher outlined what to do before the field trip.

senses.definition: What a person expects to happen or how they think about life.
senses.example: Her cheerful outlook helped the crew stay calm in the rain.

senses.definition: To be greater in number than another group.
senses.example: At the pond, the ducks outnumbered the geese.

senses.definition: A number, fact, or signal that comes out after a rule or device does its work.
senses.example: When the machine doubled four, the output was eight.

senses.definition: To run or move faster or farther than someone or something else.
senses.example: The puppy could outrun me across the yard.

senses.definition: The outer edge, surface, or part of something.
senses.example: The outside of the cup felt warm.

senses.definition: In or toward the open air or a place beyond a boundary.
senses.example: The children went outside after lunch.

senses.definition: Beyond the space or limit of something.
senses.example: We waited outside the music room.

senses.definition: To do better than someone by thinking more cleverly.
senses.example: I hoped to outsmart my brother by hiding the clue in a book.

senses.definition: A rounded shape that is longer in one direction than the other, like a drawn outline of an egg.
senses.example: We traced an oval for the face in our picture.

senses.definition: Shaped like an oval.
senses.example: The toy car followed an oval track.

senses.definition: A course that curves back to its starting point in a long rounded shape.
senses.example: The runners made two laps of the oval track.

senses.definition: Above something, sometimes moving across it.
senses.example: A bridge stretches over the river.

senses.definition: More than a certain number or amount.
senses.example: The book has over a hundred pages.

senses.definition: Finished or no longer happening.
senses.example: The rain was over by the time we got home.

senses.definition: Again and again.
senses.example: We tried the last line of the song over and over until it sounded right.

senses.definition: Over the side of a boat or ship into the water.
senses.example: A wave knocked the empty bucket overboard.

senses.definition: Covered by clouds, especially when the whole sky is gray.
senses.example: The sky was overcast, but it did not rain on our picnic.

senses.definition: To deal with a problem or strong feeling and get past it.
senses.example: I overcame my fear of speaking by practicing with a friend.

senses.definition: To spill over the top of a container or beyond the edge of a space.
senses.example: The rain barrel overflowed when it got full.

senses.definition: To hear something that was not meant for you to hear.
senses.example: I overheard two students talking about the missing ball.

senses.definition: To lie on top of part of something else or share part of the same time or area.
senses.example: The two circles overlap in the center of my drawing.

senses.definition: To put a greater load on something than it can handle.
senses.example: We overloaded the little wagon, so one wheel sank into the snow.

senses.definition: To fail to notice or consider something.
senses.example: I overlooked one spelling mistake in my first draft.

senses.definition: To have a view from above or across an area.
senses.example: Our window overlooked the playground.

senses.definition: During a night or from one evening to the next morning.
senses.example: Our wet boots dried overnight by the door.

senses.definition: Time spent working after the hours someone normally works.
senses.example: The crew worked overtime to finish painting the hall.

senses.definition: Extra time added to a game because the score is tied.
senses.example: Our team scored a goal in overtime.

senses.definition: To need to pay or give something because of a promise, loan, or what someone did for you.
senses.example: I owe Kai two dollars for my share of the snack.

senses.definition: Belonging to or connected with the person already mentioned.
senses.example: Every player brought their own water bottle.

senses.definition: To have something that belongs to you.
senses.example: Our family owns one car and three bicycles.

senses.definition: A gas in air that your body needs, carried from the lungs by blood.
senses.example: When you breathe in, some oxygen enters your blood.

senses.definition: A sea animal with a soft body protected by two shell halves that close together.
senses.example: A broken oyster shell lay beside a smooth pebble.
